title: Calm Sleeps in the Harbor...
text:
Calm sleeps in the harbor

beneath its lacquer quilt,

while the moon in the sky

drives in its golden anchors.


Heart,

row!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the compact nautical image and the sudden command to the heart.

title: The God in Whom I Believe Beats in Conscience...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the creed-like compression of conscience, creation, and ethical doctrine.

title: Song for the Eyes
text:
What I want to know

is where I am...

Where I was,

I know I will never know.

Where I am going I already know...


Where I was,

where I am going,

where I am,

I want to know,

for open upon the air,

dead, I will not know that, alive,

I am what I wanted to be.


Today I would like to see it;

not tomorrow:

Today!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the urgent self-questioning and the source's difficult dead/alive turn.

title: Dream
text:
I called you. You called me.

We sprang up like rivers.

In the sky there rose

the mingled names.


I called you. You called me.

We sprang up like rivers.

Our bodies remained

face to face, empty.


I called you. You called me.

We sprang up like rivers.

Between our two bodies,

what an unforgettable abyss!
editorial_note: The translation preserves the repeated call-and-response and the abyss between bodies.

title: I Closed My Door to the World
text:
I closed my door to the world;

my flesh was lost to me through dream...

I remained inward, magical, invisible,

naked as a blind man.


Filled to the very rim of my eyes,

I lit myself from within.


Trembling, transparent,

I remained upon the wind,

like a clean glass

of pure water,

like an angel of glass

in a mirror.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the inward illumination and the glasslike vulnerability of the closing image.
